identity.title: Herschel and ALMA Observations of Massive SZE-selected Clusters

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present new *Herschel* observations of four massive, Sunyaev-Zel’dovich Effect (SZE)-selected clusters at $0.3 \leq z \leq 1.1$, two of which have also been observed with ALMA.

distance_source.value: spectroscopic redshift from Sifón et al. 2013 (cite: 2013ApJ...772...25S)

question.value: How do star formation, cold gas and dust, and AGN content of galaxies in massive SZE-selected clusters at 0.3<z<1.1 depend on redshift and clustercentric radius, and compare to field galaxies?

evidence.quote: Questions of how cluster galaxies evolve at intermediate redshifts can be comprehensively answered by studying both their star formation *and* their gas/dust properties.
We have obtained new ALMA Cycle 2 observations (Program 2013.1.01358.S; PI: Baker)
Band 6 observations were taken between 2015 January 3 and 2015 April 6.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Two adjacent 1.875 GHz SPWs (15.625 MHz resolution) per sideband; J0102 centered 246.6 and 262.6 GHz, J0546 223.2 and 238.2 GHz

evidence.quote: The spectral window pairs spanned 3.75 GHz and were centered at 246.6 GHz and 262.6 GHz for J0102
For J0102, 35 available antennas provided baseline lengths ranging from 42 m to 1082 m.
which yielded a synthesized beam of $\sim 1.58\ensuremath{''} \times 0.98\ensuremath{''}$ ($1.85\ensuremath{''} \times 1.08\ensuremath{''}$)

sensitivity.value: Continuum 1 sigma 0.11 (J0102), 0.09 (J0546) mJy/beam; line cube 1.5 (J0102), 1.0 (J0546) mJy/beam per 50 MHz channel

evidence.quote: a $1~\sigma$ continuum sensitivity of $0.11\ \rm mJy~ beam^{-1}$ ($0.09\ \rm mJy~ beam^{-1}$) for J0102 (J0546)

time_on_source.value: Mosaics of 150 (J0102) and 142 (J0546) pointings, ~40 s per pointing

evidence.quote: Each pointing received $\sim 40$ seconds of integration time.
Band 6 observations were taken between 2015 January 3 and 2015 April 6.
We have obtained new ALMA Cycle 2 observations (Program 2013.1.01358.S; PI: Baker)

provided.value: PACS 100 and 160 um imaging (new); SPIRE from Lindner et al. 2015

evidence.quote: PACS 100 and 160 $\mu$m images were produced using version 10.3.0 of HIPE

provided.value: 2.1 GHz radio continuum from Lindner et al. 2015

evidence.quote: We use Australia Telescope Compact Array (ATCA) continuum observations centered at 2.1 GHz as presented by (cite: 2015ApJ...803...79L).

provided.value: optical imaging for astrometry and morphology

evidence.quote: We make use of *HST*/ACS F625W, F775W, F850LP images of J0102 (cite: 2013ApJ...770L..15Z)

provided.value: 3.6 and 4.5 um photometry for stellar masses

evidence.quote: we also include *Spitzer*/IRAC 3.6 and 4.5 $\mu$m observations to complement optical photometry and spectroscopy

what.value: Optical spectroscopic cluster member catalogs and redshifts

evidence.quote: Spectroscopic redshifts and numbers of spectroscopically confirmed members ($N_{\rm gal}$) from (cite: 2013ApJ...772...25S).
Dynamical mass estimates ($M_{\rm 200c}$) from (cite: 2016MNRAS.461..248S).
(cite: 2013MNRAS.435.3469H) have estimated stellar mass ($M_{\ast}$) from 3.6 $\mu$m photometry

what.value: Infrared SED template library used for L_IR fits

evidence.quote: Herschel* and ALMA continuum observations are fit to (cite: 2015ApJ...814....9K) infrared SED templates

pipeline_or_manual.value: J0102 manual reduction; J0546 ALMA pipeline, with tweaked default settings

evidence.quote: We manually reduced the J0102 data using CASA version 4.3.1
The J0546 data were automatically reduced by the ALMA pipeline, which used CASA version 4.2.2

flux_calibrator.value: J0102: Uranus; J0546: Ganymede and Callisto

evidence.quote: Ganymede and Callisto were used for flux calibration.
were produced using the standard deconvolution task in CASA, `clean`.
Both clusters were continuum imaged with natural weighting
Continuum-subtracted spectral line cubes were also imaged with natural weighting and with 50 MHz channel widths.
The synthesized beam size is $1.5 \ensuremath{''} \times 1.0\ensuremath{''}$ ($1.9\ensuremath{''} \times 1.1 \ensuremath{''}$) for J0102 (J0546)

what.value: Optical spectroscopy, SPIRE and ATCA data, PACS source-extraction matched filter

evidence.quote: SPIRE 250, 350, and 500 $\mu$m observations of our clusters were introduced in (cite: 2015ApJ...803...79L).

what.value: SFR from IR luminosity following Kennicutt & Evans

evidence.quote: Finally, we follow (cite: 2012ARA&A..50..531K) in deriving SFR from IR luminosity assuming a Chabrier initial mass function

unstated_but_needed: Which CASA clean parameters (cell size, image size, niter, threshold, mosaic gridder, masks) were used
Line-free channels used for continuum subtraction
Exact flagging/pipeline modifications beyond edge-channel flagging
Self-calibration was or was not applied
SoFiA parameter files beyond SNR 5 and 3x3 smoothing
Number of PACS sources used and cut definitions for stacks beyond 4 MAD

method.value: Manual (J0102) or pipeline (J0546) calibration in CASA; natural-weighted clean continuum images and 50 MHz line cubes

evidence.quote: Continuum images and data cubes centered on the CO and \[C I\] lines were produced using the standard deconvolution task in CASA, `clean`.

validation.value: ALMA positions compared with HST counterparts (offset 0.34 arcsec for CO, 0.26 arcsec for continuum)

evidence.quote: we find offsets of $0\ensuremath{''}{}34$ (six sources).

analysis_steps.goal: Detect line sources and measure fluxes

method.value: SoFiA search of cubes, validated against optical counterparts; fluxes via IMFIT on moment-zero maps; upper limits 3x rms for 300 km/s width

evidence.quote: We use a SNR threshold of 5.0 and smooth over 3 channels and 3 spatial pixels with Gaussian kernels.

key_parameters.value: SNR threshold 5.0; fiducial line width 300 km/s

evidence.quote: fiducial line width of $\Delta v = 300~\rm km~s^{-1}$

validation.value: Searched negative (-1x) cubes to estimate false detections

evidence.quote: we roughly estimate the number of false detections by extracting “sources” from versions of each data cube that have been multiplied by $-1$.

method.value: M_mol from CO(4-3) via Galactic X_CO and r41=0.4; M_ISM from continuum via dust-to-gas scaling law

evidence.quote: We use a dust-to-gas scaling law (equation 8.26) from (cite: 2013seg..book..491S) to convert the ALMA continuum flux density into a total gas mass

key_parameters.value: beta = 1.8; r_4,1 = 0.4; 0.3 dex added uncertainty on M_mol

evidence.quote: $\beta = 1.8$ parameterizes the dust absorption coefficient $\kappa \propto \nu^{-\beta}$
assuming a Galactic $X_{\rm CO} = 2\times10^{20} \rm~cm^{-2}~(K~km~s^{-1})^{-1}$ conversion factor

analysis_steps.goal: Fit IR SEDs for L_IR and SFR

method.value: Fit 160 um PACS flux to Kirkpatrick+15 templates by chi2 with free normalization; emcee for normalization uncertainty; SFR = 1.65 Msun/yr x L_IR/1e10 Lsun

evidence.quote: In order to find the best fitting template, $\chi^2$ is minimized while the overall SED normalization is allowed to vary as a free parameter.
we approximate $L_{\rm TIR}(3-1100~\ensuremath{\mu}m) \approx 1.1\times L_{\rm IR}(8-1000~\ensuremath{\mu}m)$

fitting.value: emcee MCMC on normalization; posterior checked as normal; sigma taken as std

evidence.quote: For each galaxy, we verify that the samples follow a normal distribution.

validation.value: Compared with Chary & Elbaz templates and ALMA continuum predictions; PACS negative-map fidelity test

evidence.quote: Only a single 4 $\sigma$ detection is found in the negative J0438 100 $\mu$m map

method.value: Bootstrap stacking of PACS, ALMA continuum, ATCA and ALMA spectra at member positions with 4 MAD outlier cut; compare to blank-sky

evidence.quote: We use bootstrapping (with replacement) to calculate stacking uncertainties or confidence intervals.
(with 5000 resampling iterations)
In every case, $p > 0.1$

analysis_steps.goal: Radio AGN diagnosis and evolution trends

method.value: q_IR from L_IR and 1.4 GHz luminosity (alpha=0.8), threshold 1.8; power-law/linear fits with emcee for IRBG fraction and sSFR vs z

evidence.loc: 5.5 The FIR-radio correlation and AGN fraction
evidence.quote: a separator of $q_{\rm IR} \approx 1.8$ is sometimes used to differentiate between star-forming galaxies and AGNs
assuming $S_\nu \propto \nu^{-\alpha}$ with spectral index $\alpha = 0.8$

fitting.value: chi2 MAP power-law then emcee sampling of index; 68% binomial intervals

evidence.quote: We sample the marginalized distribution of the power-law index parameter using `emcee`.

used_for.value: ALMA calibration, clean imaging, IMFIT flux measurement

evidence.quote: We manually reduced the J0102 data using CASA version 4.3.1

used_for.value: Spectral line source finding in cubes

evidence.quote: We use the Source Finding Application package (cite: 2015MNRAS.448.1922S) to search for spectral line sources in the ALMA data cubes.

used_for.value: MCMC posteriors for SED normalization and trends

evidence.quote: we use `emcee`, a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) code (cite: 2013PASP..125..306F)
PACS 100 and 160 $\mu$m images were produced using version 10.3.0 of HIPE
*Spitzer* catalogs are produced using the `SExtractor` software
The mean \[C I\]/CO line ratio is $0.19 \pm 0.07$ in brightness temperature units

evidence.quote: $\log (M_{\rm ISM}/M_\ensuremath{\odot}) < 10.0$ for J0102 and $\log (M_{\rm ISM}/M_\ensuremath{\odot}) < 9.9$ for J0546
$\log (M_{\rm mol}/M_\ensuremath{\odot}) < 9.8$ in both J0102 and J0546

evidence.quote: average $\log({\rm sSFR / yr}^{-1}) = -10.36 \pm 0.57$

evidence.loc: 6.2 Gas mass, infrared luminosity, and gas depletion timescale
evidence.quote: The mean $M_{\rm mol}/M_{\rm ISM}$ ratio in J0546 is $0.55^{+0.58}_{-0.34}$.

results_numeric.quantity: Mean q_IR of radio detections excluding AGN

evidence.loc: 5.5 The FIR-radio correlation and AGN fraction
evidence.quote: we find a mean $q_{\rm IR} = 1.54 \pm 0.22$

results_numeric.quantity: Mean gas fraction of CO detections

evidence.loc: 5.6 Star formation rate as a function of environment?
evidence.quote: The mean gas fraction is $f_{\rm gas} = 0.22$.

evidence.quote: The average depletion time for our sample is $\tau_{\rm dep} \sim 2~$Gyr.
implying an AGN fraction $f_{\rm AGN} \gtrsim 0.2$ for our PACS-selected sample

findings_qualitative.value: No ALMA continuum or line stacked detections; dust-continuum detections only in J0546.

evidence.quote: We do not detect significant stacked ALMA dust continuum or spectral line emission

findings_qualitative.value: IRBG fraction and sSFR increase with redshift; SFR-radius trend vanishes after normalizing by stellar mass.

evidence.quote: The fraction of infrared-bright galaxies (IRBGs; $\log (L_{\rm IR}/L_\ensuremath{\odot}) > 10.6$) per cluster and average sSFR rise significantly with redshift.

claims.hypothesis: Is the [C I]/CO ratio in cluster galaxies like that in field galaxies?
claims.experiment: Measured [C I] and CO(4-3) fluxes in ALMA detections

evidence.quote: consistent with previous results for field samples

claims.hypothesis: Do IR-bright galaxy fraction and sSFR evolve with redshift in massive clusters?
claims.experiment: Binomial fractions and emcee fits across four clusters
claims.result: p<0.005 for IRBG evolution; slope of sSFR positive at p<0.001

evidence.quote: we find that $p < 0.005$ for a zero or negative slope

claims.hypothesis: Does L_IR depend on clustercentric radius due to environment?
claims.experiment: Compared L_IR and sSFR vs radius
claims.result: L_IR trend vanishes when normalized by mass

evidence.loc: 5.6 Star formation rate as a function of environment?
evidence.quote: The relationship between star formation and radius seen in Figure [2](#fig:L_IR with environment) has completely vanished once we normalize the SFR by mass.

claims.hypothesis: Do cluster members host a high AGN fraction?

evidence.loc: 5.5 The FIR-radio correlation and AGN fraction
evidence.quote: Four out of the 19 *Herschel* detections in our study have $q_{\rm IR} < 1.8$

why_this_method.value: Stellar mass from 3.6 um rather than SED fitting because optical coverage is incomplete and would bias with radius

evidence.quote: We choose not to employ optical and NIR spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting because our optical wavelength observations do not sufficiently cover all cluster galaxies

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Chary & Elbaz templates rejected because they underestimate cold dust (0.3 dex lower L_IR)

evidence.quote: $L_{\rm IR}$ derived using (cite: 2001ApJ...556..562C) templates is systematically 0.3 dex lower

limitations_admitted.value: Optical selection of members may bias the star-forming census; small samples of CO detections.

evidence.loc: 5.3 Biases from optical selection of cluster members
evidence.quote: we have grounds for concern that our optical selection induces a general bias in our search for dust-obscured galaxies

referee_caveats_inferred: Galactic X_CO and fixed r41=0.4 dominate mass uncertainty; alternatives change masses by factors of several
Single-band (160 um) SED fits give large L_IR and q_IR uncertainties
Small number statistics (6 CO detections; IRBG counts)
Some [C I] and CO detections are marginal
